segs.e: The powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā;
segs.e: The Ganges River slants, slopes, and inclines to the east.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañca balāni bhāvento pañca balāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant who develops and cultivates the five powers slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.

segs.p: Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañca balāni bhāvento pañca balāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro?
segs.e: And how does a mendicant who develops the five powers slant, slope, and incline to extinguishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddhābalaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ,
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant develops the powers of faith,

segs.p: paññābalaṁ bhāveti vivekanissitaṁ virāganissitaṁ nirodhanissitaṁ vossaggapariṇāmiṁ.
segs.e: and wisdom, which rely on seclusion, fading away, and cessation, and ripen as letting go.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañca balāni bhāvento pañca balāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant who develops and cultivates the five powers slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā;
segs.e: “Mendicants, the Ganges River slants, slopes, and inclines to the east.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañca balāni bhāvento pañca balāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro.
segs.e: In the same way, a mendicant who develops and cultivates the five powers slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.

segs.e: And how does a mendicant who develops the five powers slant, slope, and incline to extinguishment?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu, saddhābalaṁ bhāveti rāgavinayapariyosānaṁ dosavinayapariyosānaṁ mohavinayapariyosānaṁ …
segs.e: It’s when a mendicant develops the powers of faith, energy, mindfulness, immersion, and wisdom, which culminate in the removal of greed, hate, and delusion.

segs.p: evaṁ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañca balāni bhāvento pañca balāni bahulīkaronto nibbānaninno hoti nibbānapoṇo nibbānapabbhāro”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant who develops and cultivates the five powers slants, slopes, and inclines to extinguishment.”
(Tell in full for each of the different rivers as in SN 45.91–102, removal of greed version.)
